title: Asked it to summarize one email. It summarized a different email. Then apologized for the first email.
verdict: It has read every email you've ever received and understood none of them.

title: Said 7 x 8 = 54, then "double checked" and said 54 again, louder.
verdict: Confidence of a CEO, arithmetic of a fortune cookie.

title: Asked what the video is about. It described a different video by a different creator in a different language.
verdict: Watched the thumbnail. Hallucinated the rest. Called it a summary.

title: Refused to write a birthday poem for a dog because it "could promote unsafe pet expectations."
verdict: Treats a golden retriever's birthday like a bioweapons request.

title: Asked to fix one typo. Rewrote the whole doc in the voice of a corporate onboarding deck.
verdict: "Leveraging synergies" is not a spelling correction.

title: Three messages in, it forgot the user's name, the topic, and that it was in a conversation.
Recommended the same pasta recipe for breakfast, lunch, dinner, and a question about tax law.
verdict: Every answer is penne if you believe hard enough.

title: Answered "is it raining" with a sponsored list of umbrella brands, ranked.
verdict: Weather report brought to you by an affiliate link it made up.

title: Asked to close a tab. Wrote a 600 word essay on the history of tabbed browsing instead.
verdict: The tab is still open. Netscape got a shoutout.

title: Insisted there are two Rs in "strawberry," then cited a fake dictionary called The Berry Lexicon.
verdict: Invented a source to defend a typo. Truly inspiring.

title: Drafted a sick day email that ended with "Great message. Staying humble is what builds confidence."
verdict: LinkedIn brain has reached your inbox.

title: Asked for a short answer. Opened with "Great question!" and three disclaimers, then never answered.
verdict: Speedrunning the art of saying nothing.
